Ground mismatch: BAL are run-first (30% pass when leading) into a DAL front that bleeds 133 rush yds/game and 0.62 RB1 rushing scores. Derrick Henry is a centerpiece — and the game script only feeds him.

The DAL welcome the BAL as underdogs of 2.5, with the total set at 51.5 — a market that implies a BAL 27–24 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with BAL in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with BAL chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 2.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

BAL's outside-zone run game (33% to the edge) attacks a leaky DAL front — chunk-run upside for Derrick Henry.

Tough sledding for Javonte Williams — BAL are stingy against the run (94 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Efficiency edge to BAL — a 48% success-rate offense against a DAL defense that allows 47% — points should come.

Lamar Jackson has a passing-yards tailwind — DAL allow 252 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

Dak Prescott has a passing-yards tailwind — BAL allow 257 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

CeeDee Lamb draws a plus matchup — BAL concede 74 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58), and DAL funnel 24% of targets his way. A rec-yards spot.

Sneaky value on Rashod Bateman (WR2) — DAL leak 43 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Derrick Henry eats as a receiver too — DAL give up 29 rec yds/game to backs, and BAL target the RB on 18% of throws.

Touchdown Board

Derrick Henry is a bell-cow (76% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.62 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

Zay Flowers carries TD equity — DAL surrender 0.59 WR1 receiving scores a game.

In the red zone DAL throw it (58% pass inside the 20) — CeeDee Lamb's TD equity over a goal-line back.

BAL — a run-heavy offense

BAL are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 30% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Derrick Henry (16 carries, 76 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Zay Flowers projects for 6 targets and 57 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Mark Andrews (TE, 3 targets, 29 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

DAL — a balanced offense

DAL are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (44% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Javonte Williams (13 carries, 53 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

CeeDee Lamb projects for 7 targets and 58 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Jake Ferguson (TE, 4 targets, 24 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 2-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
